<a id="计数是关系--counting-is-a-relation"></a>
# Counting is a relation

<!-- Generated by build_result_registry.py; edit the matching JSON record. -->

> A count exists exactly where what it counts is decided, and a decision procedure's marks are the count; the census between counts needs no decidedness.

<a id="主张-claim"></a>
## Claim

A proposition is decided (Decided) where it holds or fails; a decision procedure (Decidable) gives this as data, the core's logic does not assume it of every proposition, and that a proposition is decided cannot be refuted (not_not_decided). A number indicates a proposition (Indicates) where it is one and the proposition holds, or zero and it fails; a number counts the members of a list of which a determination holds (Counts) where it sums their indicators; across a list of steps, the counts at each step sum (CountsAcross). Something indicates a proposition exactly where the proposition is decided (indicates_iff_decided), and a count of a list exists exactly where each member is decided (counts_iff_decided); a count is one number (Counts.unique), at most the members (Counts.le_length), and where a procedure decides, its marks are the count (counts_total, comings_counts, ceasings_counts). The census between counts needs no decidedness: over a stretch, wherever the counts exist, those holding at the end with those that ceased are those holding at the start with those that came to be (Counts.over_stretch), with no decidedness even at the steps inside the stretch: decided there, the census holds (Counts.over_stretch_decided), that finitely many states are all decided cannot be refuted, and an equation of numbers holds wherever its failure is refuted. Likewise across one step (Counts.across_step), and comings and ceasings differ by at most the members (CountsAcross.keep_pace). Where what holds is listed at each step, each member once, the lists give the census with no decidedness either (Counts.listed_across, Counts.listed_over_stretch): a count is the length of a list of the members counted (Counts.listing), and two lists without repetition with the same members are equally long (length_eq_of_same). No ethical premise and no Lean axiom is used.

Canonical source: [Decidedness.lean](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Decidedness.lean)

<a id="前提与对应-hypotheses-and-correspondence"></a>
## Hypotheses and correspondence

- The laws of counting: the counts exist (Counts); the steps inside the stretch need not be decided.
- The listed forms: what holds is listed at each step, each member once (Listed).
- Discrete steps; finite lists.

Ren, 11 October 2026: “give me more context, but i intuitively feel decidability is too dualist, also proved solutions and their pro/cons”, and “please” to the AI's suggestion that decidability be made local, no longer a commitment of the representation (zero-premise plan, section 1.4 (b2)). The AI's reading: “too dualist” is the yes/no split imposed on becoming; “local” is at the states counted only, as that law's own condition. The laws between counts hold of whatever counts exist, without asking that they exist; a statement that needs a count states decidedness as its condition, at what it counts. The reading is adopted on Ren's delegation.

## Validation and boundaries

Successful Lean 4.29.1 consolidated check (20261013T094743.528770Z): the 55 theorems of Becoming.Decidedness all have empty axiom reports; the same receipt covers the package's 75 modules (including the import-only root and the bridge) with 4518 theorems/6370 declaration audits, and 22 inherited modules whose current bytes match passed receipts; periphery receipt 20261013T095049.338744Z passed. The checker also verifies core purity: the import closure of the core (GenerativeCore, InquirySufficiency, RelationalRenewal, L1–L4 and the root module Becoming) is exactly these 77 modules, every source declaration in it has an empty axiom report (of the constants Lean generates, only the injectivity lemmas of constructors with fields, injEq, depend on propext; no source declaration uses them, and the checker lists them), and it compiles from Lean's prelude alone (the foundation's import Std removed for that run). The author's counterreview is in §84 of the integration note; not yet independently reviewed.

A count existing needs what it counts to be decided, a theorem (counts_iff_decided), not a premise on worlds; theorems whose statements count by mark keep a decision procedure as their own condition, listed on the inventory page; stated for discrete steps and finite lists; the readings are the AI's, adopted on Ren's delegation.

- The undecided world (World.undecided) is finite, with arising recurring (World.undecided_world); a law giving ceasing recurring from arising recurring in every finite world decides any proposition Q at undecided Q (World.law_decides), so asking the recurrence law of every finite world without decidedness is excluded middle (World.law_iff_em): the laws between counts need no decidedness, the exact form of recurrence does. The need comes only from activity being a proposition, which undecided Q sets to an arbitrary Q at one step: a calibration of the representation's logic, a lemma of the decided law, saying nothing further about change. <a id="依赖与关联-dependencies-and-related-results"></a>
## Dependencies and related results

- **formal-reuse**: [coming-and-ceasing-keep-pace](coming-and-ceasing-keep-pace.md). Reuses coming to be and ceasing (ComesToBe, CeasesToBe) and their counts by a decision procedure's marks (mark, comings, ceasings).

**Output:** Coming to be and ceasing across a step, and their counts by marks.

**Input:** Where a procedure decides, its marks sum to the count (counts_total, comings_counts, ceasings_counts); a count as a relation, existing exactly where what it counts is decided.

**Preserved conditions:** A decision procedure (counts_total, comings_counts and ceasings_counts only). [Change.lean](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Change.lean)

- Related, not a proved adapter: [recurrence-without-decidedness](recurrence-without-decidedness.md). The same module: the laws of recurrence without decidedness.
- Related, not a proved adapter: [census-balance](census-balance.md). There, with what holds listed at each step, the census balance is counted by marks (Listed.across, Listed.over_stretch); here the same census holds between counts, with no decidedness (Counts.listed_across, Counts.listed_over_stretch, Counts.over_stretch).
- Related, not a proved adapter: [whole-law-of-counting](whole-law-of-counting.md). There the laws count by marks; here a count is a relation, existing exactly where what it counts is decided, so counting by marks is counting where decided.

**Used by:** [listing-once-is-decided-identity](listing-once-is-decided-identity.md) · [negation-change-and-stable-cases](negation-change-and-stable-cases.md)

**Law family:** The census and the laws of counting (lead: [census-balance](census-balance.md)). What comes to be and what ceases are counted against one list: the list at the end with what ceased is the list at the start with what came. The members state that balance and its halves (ceasing needs arising; under a continuation, a bounded census and enclosure), where the counts exist (where what they count is decided), the census read off the exchange, and what the premises add to the tally.
